audit.signed_message_spec: sha256(run_id \x00 merkle_root \x00 findings_count \x00 header_canonical) — the 32-byte digest; the Ed25519 signature covers the digest
audit.recipe:
INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION RECIPE (open tools only, no code access):
1) For each verified finding record in report.findings, compute leaf_i = sha256(canonical(record)) where canonical = JSON with SORTED keys, separators (',', ':'), UTF-8, and the declared volatile keys (notes, durations, wall times, stats, requests...) removed recursively at every depth.
2) Build the Merkle tree: pair leaves bottom-up, node = sha256(left || right); when a level has an ODD count, duplicate its last hash once. The empty findings set has the root sha256(b'') = e3b0c44298fc1c14...55. The result must equal report.audit.merkle_root.
3) Compute the signed message digest: sha256 of the four fields joined by a single 0x00 byte each: run_id, merkle_root, findings_count, then the canonical header JSON {'run_id','seed','scanner','target'} (sorted keys, compact).
4) Verify the Ed25519 signature (RFC 8032) of that digest with the embedded public key (report.audit.public_key_b64, 32 raw bytes): python cryptography: Ed25519PublicKey.from_public_bytes(base64.b64decode(public_key_b64)).verify(base64.b64decode(signature_b64), digest); openssl: build the SPKI PEM 302a300506032b6570032100||pubkey and run openssl pkeyutl -verify -pubin -inkey pub.pem -rawin -in msg.bin -sig sig.bin. Any mismatch in (2) or (4) means the report was altered after signing — tampering is DETECTED, not trusted.
